detail:
Refinement to the D13 assessment after the store-measurement correction (78/89 empty-affected_files decisions carry provenance.commit_sha on the authoritative mirror).

Design conclusion inverts the investigating agent's original recommendation: retroactive derivation over provenance.commit_sha clears the existing backlog on its own (~90% yield), making it the PRIMARY mechanism; capturing the discarded diff at record-tools.ts:48 fixes the forward path (no git resolution needed at all). Complementary, not competing — build both, derivation first.

The parent-sha trap gets SHARPER at 90% coverage: every stored sha is the commit BEFORE the work (Gate 2 records pre-commit). A derivation reading them directly produces confidently wrong file edges at ~90% coverage — strictly worse than today's 0%, because it is silent and the edges look declared-quality. Requirements for whatever lands: (1) child-commit resolution, e.g. git log --ancestry-path <sha>..HEAD | tail -1; (2) explicit bail when the record→commit pairing is not 1:1; (3) the bail case is exactly where the ask-4 inferred marker must carry a CONFIDENCE signal, not just a source label — plan the marker vocabulary accordingly (e.g. derivation: "commit-provenance", confidence: "exact"|"ambiguous").

Process note for the audit trail: the original low-yield estimate came from reading the stale v1 store (.twining/decisions/, last written Jul 5) instead of the sqlite mirror — the same staleness tell the agent had already caught for graph relations one lane over. When counting on this repo, always use .twining/records/ or the db, never the v1 directories.
summary: D13 addendum: build both fixes, derivation first — backlog via commit_sha (child-commit resolution + 1:1 bail required), forward via capturing discarded diff; naive derivation worse than none
